samples.summary: No test covers a per-item record that carries no `latency` object — the denominator silently shrinks and the completeness guard cannot fire
samples.evidence: `coderabbitLatency` builds `lats = perItem.map((it) => it?.latency).filter(Boolean)` (cost-latency.mjs:632) and then reports `n_items: lats.length` (line 652). The completeness shortfall at cost-latency.mjs:797 compares `latency.self_timed.n < latency.n_items`, i.e. against a denominator that has ALREADY dropped every item whose adapter read produced no latency at all. So a run where 3 of 7 items came back without a `latency` key reports "4 of 4 poolable", raises no reason, and stays `verdict: "complete"`. Every fixture row in the new tests carries a full `latency` (test file lines 134-148); the only degraded case tested (`a missing start marker…`, line 551) keeps the `latency` object and only nulls `self_timed.ms`, which is exactly the path that DOES fire the guard. Nothing in cost-latency.test.mjs passes a record shaped `{item_id, latency: null}` or `{item_id}`.
searchedFor: grep for `latency: null` / `latencyRow(` in the test file
read latencyOf/corpusRecords in adapters/coderabbit.mjs to confirm the field can be absent for a failed read

samples.summary: `SCHEMA_VERSION` bumped 1 → 2 with no test asserting it, unlike the sibling scorers
samples.evidence: cost-latency.mjs:97 bumps the counter and the docblock says the bump is the contract signal for `coderabbit.latency` changing from a scalar to a block. `SCHEMA_VERSION` is not imported by cost-latency.test.mjs (imports at lines 28-48) and `schema_version` is never asserted anywhere in that file, so a revert to 1 — or a future meaning change made without bumping — goes green. The convention exists in this directory: finding-record.test.mjs:257 asserts `SCHEMA_VERSION === 1`.
searchedFor: read cost-latency.test.mjs import list and full body

samples.summary: The new report's UNRECOGNISED absence branch is untested, though the analogous branches elsewhere are
samples.evidence: `renderCoderabbitLatency` marks an absence flavour not in `LATENCY_ABSENT` as `UNRECOGNISED f=n` (cost-latency.mjs:993). No test in cost-latency.test.mjs feeds a census containing an undeclared flavour — the crippled fixture (test line 552) uses the declared `no-start-marker`. The same file DOES test the equivalent for `duration_source` (test line 207, `wall-clock-v2`), and adapters/coderabbit.test.mjs:1247 tests it for its own census line, so the omission is a coverage hole rather than a convention.
searchedFor: grep UNRECOGNISED in cost-latency.test.mjs and adapters/coderabbit.test.mjs

samples.summary: New "declared gaps — none" report branch is unreachable and therefore untested
samples.evidence: renderReport line 962 adds a branch for `result.declared_gaps.length === 0`, but `declaredGaps()` always pushes `cost_per_real_finding` (line 683-691), so the array is never empty. No test asserts the string, and none can — a branch no test can drive is coverage that reads as coverage. The neighbouring test (test line 490) instead asserts the gap list is exactly `["cost_per_real_finding"]` once latency is supplied.
searchedFor: read declaredGaps and its only call sites

samples.summary: The new `--coderabbit-latency` CLI wiring (flag registration and the corpusRecords→per-item mapping) has no test
samples.evidence: cost-latency.mjs:1025 registers the boolean and lines 1087-1094 map `corpusRecords(store, corpusVersion)` to `{item_id, latency}` and feed it as `coderabbit.latency`. cost-latency.test.mjs contains no CLI invocation (no spawnSync/execFileSync; the only child-process usage in this directory's tests is test-lane.test.mjs:20, which does not run this script). A typo in the flag name, or a mapping that dropped `latency`, would leave every library test green while the flag silently produced the `requested:false` path — i.e. a declared gap where a measurement was asked for. `corpusRecords` itself is injectable (`{api, log}`) and is exercised that way in adapters/coderabbit.test.mjs:1358, so a network-free CLI-level test is feasible.

samples.summary: No test for `coderabbit.latency: []` — requested with zero records retires the gap and still reports `complete`
samples.evidence: An empty array passes `Array.isArray` (line 621), so `requested: true`, `n_items: 0`, all series n=0; the shortfall check at line 797 (`0 < 0`) never fires and `declaredGaps({latencyMeasured: true})` drops the latency gap. The result therefore claims the gap is closed while carrying no minutes, and the verdict stays `complete`. cost-latency.test.mjs only exercises the 7-row `pilotLatency()`, the crippled 7-row variant, and `null` (tests at lines 496, 517, 551, 569); no zero-length case appears.
searchedFor: read the requested/unrequested branches of coderabbitLatency

samples.summary: `assert.match(pooled, /n=7/)` cannot distinguish observation pooling from item pooling on a single-replicate fixture
samples.evidence: The POOLED OVER OBSERVATIONS assertion runs against `scoreK1()`, which has one replicate, so 7 observations and 7 items coincide and the assertion holds under either implementation. The distinguishing case is covered elsewhere (test line 620, n=21), so this is a weak assertion rather than an uncovered behaviour.

mergedFrom.summary: No test for `coderabbit.latency: []` — requested with zero records retires the gap and still reports `complete`
mergedFrom.evidence: An empty array passes `Array.isArray` (line 621), so `requested: true`, `n_items: 0`, all series n=0; the shortfall check at line 797 (`0 < 0`) never fires and `declaredGaps({latencyMeasured: true})` drops the latency gap. The result therefore claims the gap is closed while carrying no minutes, and the verdict stays `complete`. cost-latency.test.mjs only exercises the 7-row `pilotLatency()`, the crippled 7-row variant, and `null` (tests at lines 496, 517, 551, 569); no zero-length case appears.

verdict.reason: The literal absence is real — no test anywhere passes a per-item record lacking a `latency` object (all uses go through `latencyRow`, cost-latency.test.mjs:134-146, 518/538/555). But it is not a blocking test-adequacy gap, because the input shape it asks for cannot be produced in this repository. `corpusRecords` unconditionally sets `latency: latencyOf(...)` on every item (adapters/coderabbit.mjs:1144-1151) and is the only producer (cost-latency.mjs:1087-1089); `latencyOf` has no null-returning branch — a failed read degrades into a populated object carrying a named absence flavour (`findings-unavailable` :860, `issue-comments-unavailable` :904, `check-runs-unavailable` :937, span() :976-987), so such an item stays in `lats`, stays in the `n_items` denominator, and DOES trip the guard at cost-latency.mjs:797. The reviewer's stated reachability premise ("the field can be absent for a failed read") is therefore wrong, and the degraded path that actually occurs is meaningfully tested at both levels: cost-latency.test.mjs:551-567 (n=6 of 7, census flavour, verdict "partial") and coderabbit.test.mjs:1214-1237 (latencyOf with issueComments:null/checkRuns:null still yields a counted object). A missing test for an unconstructable input is a nit under this lens, not a major missing-coverage blocker.
